title: Fine-grained token timing & cache-impact attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add end-to-end attribution for per-token latency and cost that attributes observed RPC/compute time to tokens, and surfaces the impact of KV/prefix cache hits vs misses. This work ties trace hooks, metrics/log enrichment, and dashboarding together so engineers and customers can answer: how many tokens did cache save, which tokens dominated latency, and what is per-token costing under typical workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A single trace/span convention is defined and implemented that captures per-token timings for generation requests (token_index, gen_start_ns, gen_end_ns, cache_event)
Pipeline enriches existing request logs with token-level aggregate metrics (p50/p95 per-token latency, token_count, cache_hit_ratio) stored in metrics DB and available for dashboards
Dashboards in Console show token-latency waterfall, cache-hit contribution, and per-model token cost estimates, with filter by model, route, and release
Instrumentation overhead measured and limited: <5% added p95 latency in synthetic microbenchmarks and <1% increase in CPU/GPU telemetry where applicable
Rollout is gated by a feature flag and can be disabled per-tenant; migration notes and backward compatibility documented
implementation_notes: Tracing: add a lightweight ‘token-timing’ child span per 32 tokens by default to avoid trace explosion; span tags: token_start, token_end, cache_hits, kv_cache_id
Edge hook: attach sampling hint at API gateway so sampling rate can be adjusted for heavy tail routes
Runtime: expose internal per-step timers from serving runtime (kernel selection, kv lookup, attention, decode) as short integers to avoid high-cardinality strings

Metrics pipeline: aggregate token spans into per-request summaries at edge (p50/p95 per-token-index buckets), emit into Prometheus-compatible metrics and to our ClickHouse event table for long-tail queries
Storage: keep raw token-level traces for sampled requests for 72 hours, aggregated metrics retained 90 days in clickhouse for dashboards and correlation with billing
Backward compatibility: when flag off, no new spans/fields are emitted and existing schemas remain unchanged
tradeoffs: Sampling vs completeness: full-token traces give richest debugging but are expensive; we use adaptive sampling plus fixed-bucket aggregation to capture both distribution and hotspots
Span cardinality: creating a span per token spikes trace storage — we limit to per-32-token spans and rely on aggregation to represent per-token behavior
Edge aggregation increases network compute but lowers downstream storage costs — acceptable given cost targets for observability
Dashboard freshness vs retention: trade real-time token metrics (sub-5s) vs cost of high cardinality; settled on 10s rollups for console views and on-demand sub-second views for sampled traces
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement feature-flagged token aggregation with sampling=0.1 for internal orgs only; monitor overhead and storage
Phase 2 (beta): open to self-serve customers with opt-in console toggle; expose Kibana/ClickHouse queries for audits
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all customers with conservative sampling defaults and per-tenant controls; update docs and SDK notes
Rollback: feature flag off; trace parser tolerant to missing spans
testing_plan: Unit tests for trace span generation and semantic tags
Load test scenario: 10k rps generation workload with mixed seq lengths to measure overhead; compare baseline vs flag-on
Integration tests to verify aggregation pipeline writes correct clickhouse rows and prom metrics emitted
E2E validation: sample traces inspected for correct token_index and cache_event correlation
Security review for added metadata fields to ensure no PII introduced
dashboards: Token latency waterfall: per-token p50/p95 across token index buckets; filter by model/release/route
Cache impact view: stacked area showing tokens served from KV cache vs compute and the estimated cost savings
Top slow tokens: table of tokens (token_index window) contributing >1% of end-to-end latency with links to sampled traces
Cost attribution: estimate per-token compute cost using per-token-time * model-cost-per-second; shown per-route and aggregated per-customer
Regression alert: if median per-token latency increases by >15% vs baseline for 24h, create incident candidate
instrumentation_endpoints: runtime.emit_token_span(token_info)  // invoked in runtime after token decode step
tracing.on_sampled_request(callback)  // attach sampled traces to long-term storage
data_pipeline_changes: ClickHouse: new table token_metrics_v1 with columns (request_id, model, route, token_bucket, p50_ns, p95_ns, cache_hit_ratio, ts)
Prometheus: add histogram metric redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket with labels model, route, bucket_range
Log enrichment: add JSON fields token_summary and cache_counts to request logs emitted to ELK
Retention: raw token traces stored in S3 lifecycle 72h -> cold archive
